entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "With a final whistle, the Maroon Tr..."
entries.dialogueText: With a final whistle, the Maroon Train came to a stop in the middle of the Forest of October.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I opened the window to look outside..."
entries.dialogueText: I opened the window to look outside. The air was cool and I enjoyed the smell of nature for a brief moment.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I straightened my jacket as she app..."
entries.dialogueText: I straightened my jacket as she approached.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "With a haughty sniff, she turned ar..."
entries.dialogueText: With a haughty sniff, she turned around and left the wagon.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A few minutes later, another train..."
entries.dialogueText: A few minutes later, another train pulled in behind ours and stopped with a whistle.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She looked much older and more tire..."
entries.dialogueText: She looked much older and more tired than the last time I had seen her. Clearly, the war had taken its toll on her.

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Mr. Rayne.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. Rayne.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She put her hand forward."
entries.dialogueText: She put her hand forward.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I kissed her hand."
entries.dialogueText: I kissed her hand.
entries.menuText: Kiss her hand.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "We shook hands."
entries.dialogueText: We shook hands.
entries.menuText: Shake her hand.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I gestured towards the wagon."
entries.dialogueText: I gestured towards the wagon.
entries.menuText: Gesture towards the wagon.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What's wrong with being out in nat..."
entries.dialogueText: “What's wrong with being out in nature?"
entries.menuText: “What's wrong with being out in nature?"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“You couldn't have chosen a better..."
entries.dialogueText: “You couldn't have chosen a better location, could you?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You are here to sign your capitula..."
entries.dialogueText: “You are here to sign your capitulation. You will meet me wherever I please.”
entries.menuText: “You are here to sign your capitulation. You will meet me wherever I please.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Don't take me for a fool, Mr. Rayn..."
entries.dialogueText: “Don't take me for a fool, Mr. Rayne.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Shut up. I don't want to spend any..."
entries.dialogueText: “Shut up. I don't want to spend any more time than I need with you.”
entries.menuText: “Shut up. I don't want to spend any more time than I need with you.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Hah. Such vulgarity. Barbarians, a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Hah. Such vulgarity. Barbarians, all of you.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“As if your victory was not enough,..."
entries.dialogueText: “As if your victory was not enough, you felt compelled to drag me out to the middle of a forest to cement it."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“And not just any forest, of course..."
entries.dialogueText: “And not just any forest, of course.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“This is the same place where the c..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is the same place where the ceasefire was signed for the 15-Day War.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“You really are trying to humiliate..."
entries.dialogueText: “You really are trying to humiliate me, aren't you?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Of course not. This is a simple co..."
entries.dialogueText: “Of course not. This is a simple coincidence. That's all.”
entries.menuText: “Of course not. This is a simple coincidence. That's all.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Give me the bloody papers. I can't..."
entries.dialogueText: “Give me the bloody papers. I can't stand breathing the same air as you.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Ms. Livingston, you are forgetting..."
entries.dialogueText: “Ms. Livingston, you are forgetting the protocol. I expect you to say please first.”
entries.menuText: “Ms. Livingston, you are forgetting the protocol. I expect you to say please first.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You are not being a good loser, Ms..."
entries.dialogueText: “You are not being a good loser, Ms. Livingston.”
entries.menuText: “You are not being a good loser, Ms. Livingston.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“You're not only a barbarian, you'r..."
entries.dialogueText: “You're not only a barbarian, you're a liar."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Yes, I am. So what? What can you d..."
entries.dialogueText: “Yes, I am. So what? What can you do without your country, Queen of Rumburg?”
entries.menuText: “Yes, I am. So what? What can you do without your country, Queen of Rumburg?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's just get to the signing.""
entries.dialogueText: “Let's just get to the signing."
entries.menuText: “Let's just get to the signing."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She struggled to come up with a res..."
entries.dialogueText: She struggled to come up with a response, then gave up and sighed heavily.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I handed her the papers."
entries.dialogueText: I handed her the papers.
entries.menuText: Hand her the papers.

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Oh, come on. Such childish behavio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Oh, come on. Such childish behavior.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I said, say please.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I said, say please.”
entries.menuText: “I said, say please.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Please... hand me the papers, Mr...."
entries.dialogueText: “Please... hand me the papers, Mr. Rayne.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Beatrice angrily scribbled her sign..."
entries.dialogueText: Beatrice angrily scribbled her signature and put down the pen before passing on the document. I signed the agreement and gave it to my assistant.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The witnesses were called for the s..."
entries.dialogueText: The witnesses were called for the signing of the agreement titled the 'Treaty of Rayne'.

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“There you go. Are you quite satisf..."
entries.dialogueText: “There you go. Are you quite satisfied?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Yes, I am happy.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Yes, I am happy.”
entries.menuText: “Yes, I am happy.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“I'm sure you would act the same wa..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm sure you would act the same way if you were in my place."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“I hereby proclaim that you can go..."
entries.dialogueText: “I hereby proclaim that you can go fuck yourself."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I don't want to see your face agai..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't want to see your face again.”
entries.menuText: “I don't want to see your face again.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Rest assured, you will not.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Rest assured, you will not.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Before you go, there is one more t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Before you go, there is one more thing.”
entries.menuText: “Before you go, there is one more thing.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“What is it?”"
entries.dialogueText: “What is it?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Don't ever forget who your Suzerai..."
entries.dialogueText: “Don't ever forget who your Suzerain is.”
entries.menuText: “Don't ever forget who your Suzerain is.”

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“I won't forget.""
entries.dialogueText: “I won't forget."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She paused for a second and glared..."
entries.dialogueText: She paused for a second and glared at me in pure fury.

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: "“Oh, trust me...”"
entries.dialogueText: “Oh, trust me...”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "My cabin rocked gently as the Maroo..."
entries.dialogueText: My cabin rocked gently as the Maroon Train sped through the leafy outskirts of Estord.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "An assistant knocked sharply, then..."
entries.dialogueText: An assistant knocked sharply, then slid the door open. He approached my desk and handed me the day's newspaper and a letter.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The first thing I saw was the headl..."
entries.dialogueText: The first thing I saw was the headline: 'Conqueror Rayne' written in giant letters.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I took a look at the newspaper."
entries.dialogueText: I took a look at the newspaper.
entries.menuText: Read the newspaper.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I opened the letter."
entries.dialogueText: I opened the letter.
entries.menuText: Open the letter.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I continued reading."
entries.dialogueText: I continued reading.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...After the triumphant victory of..."
entries.dialogueText: "...After the triumphant victory of our soldiers, President Rayne welcomed them back home in Holsord. The entire country has broken out in celebration of Rumburg's defeat..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...Defense minister Iosef Lancea w..."
entries.dialogueText: "...Defense minister Iosef Lancea was the man of the hour as his radical pincer attack plan caught the enemy off guard. Our troops immediately broke their ranks and started marching towards Rumburg's capital..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Defense minister Iosef Lancea was..."
entries.dialogueText: "Defense minister Iosef Lancea was the man of the hour as his radical plan, in his own words, 'Maradunen Schlium', caught the enemy off guard. Our troops immediately broke their ranks and started marching towards Rumburg's capital...'

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Defense minister Iosef Lancea was..."
entries.dialogueText: "Defense minister Iosef Lancea was the man of the hour as his superior strategies broke the morale of the enemy. Our troops were victorious in their assault and tipped the scales in our favor. Soon after, they were on their way to Rumburg's capital...'

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Experts are still analyzing the pa..."
entries.dialogueText: "Experts are still analyzing the particulars of the victory, but there is one fact they agree on: The siege of Thornbourgh was the turning point that drove Rumburg into where they are now. A full and unconditional surrender...'

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...President Rayne is currently on..."
entries.dialogueText: "...President Rayne is currently on his way to sign the capitulation agreement. The historic moment will be taking place in the exact same location as the signing of the 15-Day War's ceasefire. The Forest of October..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I put down the paper to take a sip..."
entries.dialogueText: I put down the paper to take a sip from my coffee.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I recognized Franc's handwriting im..."
entries.dialogueText: I recognized Franc's handwriting immediately.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Dear Father. I hope this letter fi..."
entries.dialogueText: "Dear Father. I hope this letter finds you well."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "'I wanted to congratulate you on ou..."
entries.dialogueText: 'I wanted to congratulate you on our victory against Rumburg. We showed them who they were messing with.'

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Is that how you old folks say it?..."
entries.dialogueText: "Is that how you old folks say it? I know I could have called, but a letter felt more appropriate for the occasion."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Everyone's talking about the war h..."
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone's talking about the war here in Arcasia. I have to say it feels pretty nice being the son of the commander-in-chief of the winning side."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Everyone's talking about the war h..."
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone's talking about the war here in United Contana. I have to say it feels pretty nice being the son of the commander-in-chief of the winning side."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Everyone's talking about the war h..."
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone's talking about the war here at school. I know I complain about how hard it is being your son sometimes, but I have to say it feels pretty nice right now."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""That said... I can't help but thin..."
entries.dialogueText: "That said... I can't help but think about all the guys who died. That could've been me over there. Considering how badly I flunked my exams, it probably should've been me."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""But there's nothing I can do to ch..."
entries.dialogueText: "But there's nothing I can do to change any of that now."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "'All I can ask is this: When you se..."
entries.dialogueText: 'All I can ask is this: When you see the Queen, give her a big fat middle finger from me."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "'Best Regards, Franc Rayne.'"
entries.dialogueText: 'Best Regards, Franc Rayne.'

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "'P.S.: Mom is fine and Deana might..."
entries.dialogueText: 'P.S.: Mom is fine and Deana might have a boyfriend.'

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Smiling, I shoved the papers to the..."
entries.dialogueText: Smiling, I shoved the papers to the side of my desk. I heard another knock on my door.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The assistant let me know that we h..."
entries.dialogueText: The assistant let me know that we had almost arrived at our destination.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I stepped out of my cabin and exite..."
entries.dialogueText: I stepped out of my cabin and exited the wagon to greet my esteemed guests.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I stepped out of my cabin and exite..."
entries.dialogueText: I stepped out of my cabin and exited the wagon to await the Queen of Rumburg.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Queen Beatrice stepped out of the f..."
entries.dialogueText: Queen Beatrice stepped out of the front-most wagon.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We shook hands and waited in silenc..."
entries.dialogueText: We shook hands and waited in silence for the Queen's arrival.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We entered the train cabin where th..."
entries.dialogueText: We entered the train cabin where the signing would take place. It was dominated by a polished mahogany writing desk. I took my seat on one side of it; the Queen took hers on the other.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""I can't help but think about all m..."
entries.dialogueText: "I can't help but think about all my friends and squadmates on the front lines. I know I'm lucky to be deployed here in Holsord, but part of me wishes I could've fought with them."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Still... I wonder if you and the o..."
entries.dialogueText: "Still... I wonder if you and the other bigwigs back in Holsord know the real cost of this war. It's not just that I could've died. It's that some of the things I did make me wish I had."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""It's hard for me and the other guy..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's hard for me and the other guys to sleep at night. I can only hope the memories will go away with time."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Everyone at Camp Strongarm is talk..."
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone at Camp Strongarm is talking about the war, obviously. And they're talking about me. Not in a good way."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Please accept this pen as a remind..."
entries.dialogueText: “Please accept this pen as a reminder of this historic occasion."
entries.menuText: “Please accept this pen as a reminder of this historic occasion."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Everyone's talking about the war h..."
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone's talking about the war here in Arcasia. I have to say it feels pretty nice being part of the winning coalition."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Everyone's talking about the war h..."
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone's talking about the war here in United Contana. I have to say it feels pretty nice being part of the winning coalition."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...no matter what, Wehlen came to..."
entries.dialogueText: "...no matter what, Wehlen came to Sordland's aid in its time of need. This is definitely the start of a new and lasting alliance in the region, Wiktor Smolak proclaimed..."

entries.speaker: Patricio Alvarez
entries.title: Patricio Alvarez: "“President Rayne. Let's get this ov..."
entries.dialogueText: “President Rayne. Let's get this over with as quickly as possible.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Patricio Alvarez stepped out of the..."
entries.dialogueText: Patricio Alvarez stepped out of the wagon next to mine.

entries.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
entries.title: Emmerich Hegel: "“President Rayne. Let's get this ov..."
entries.dialogueText: “President Rayne. Let's get this over with as quickly as possible.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Emmerich Hegel stepped out of the w..."
entries.dialogueText: Emmerich Hegel stepped out of the wagon next to mine.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Maartin Van Hoorten arrived at the..."
entries.dialogueText: Maartin Van Hoorten arrived at the clearing near the tracks.

entries.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
entries.title: Maartin Van Hoorten: "“Mr. President. The time has finall..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. President. The time has finally come.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Wiktor Smolak walked over with his..."
entries.dialogueText: Wiktor Smolak walked over with his arms open. He was smiling.

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: "“I can't wait to see the look of de..."
entries.dialogueText: “I can't wait to see the look of defeat on her face.”

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: "“Anton! My friend! It's certainly b..."
entries.dialogueText: “Anton! My friend! It's certainly been a long ride but finally, we are here.”

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: "“Anton! My friend! It's certainly b..."
entries.dialogueText: “Anton! My friend! It's certainly been a long ride but finally, we are here.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...Lespia leader Patricio Alvarez..."
entries.dialogueText: "...Lespia leader Patricio Alvarez raised his fist alongside President Rayne after the victory parade in a display of unity..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...Valgsland leader Emmerich Hegel..."
entries.dialogueText: "...Valgsland leader Emmerich Hegel raised his fist alongside President Rayne after the victory parade in a display of unity..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""...PM Maartin Van Hoorten proclaim..."
entries.dialogueText: "...PM Maartin Van Hoorten proclaimed that peace had finally arrived in Eastern Merkopa..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I remembered the jubilant welcome c..."
entries.dialogueText: I remembered the jubilant welcome ceremony and smiled. I flipped the page.

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Part I ... Section II ... Reparati..."
entries.dialogueText: "Part I ... Section II ... Reparations ... "

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The witnesses were called for the s..."
entries.dialogueText: The witnesses were called for the signing of the agreement titled the 'Treaty of Estord'.

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Sordland's government affirms and..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sordland's government affirms and the Rumburg accepts the responsibility of Rumburg for causing for the losses and damages..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You want us to pay reparations for..."
entries.dialogueText: "You want us to pay reparations for a war that you declared!"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Section V... Sordland's Front...""
entries.dialogueText: "Section V... Sordland's Front..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""This is outrageous!""
entries.dialogueText: "This is outrageous!"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Rumburg will immediately surrender..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rumburg will immediately surrender the cities of Tzarsbourgh, Dome, and their respective surrounding territories..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You want our two major cities in t..."
entries.dialogueText: "You want our two major cities in the south? This will cripple us for years to come."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Ms. Livingston, it seems you are n..."
entries.dialogueText: “Ms. Livingston, it seems you are not fully comprehending the situation. I am not asking!”
entries.menuText: “Ms. Livingston, it seems you are not fully comprehending the situation. I am not asking!”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Ms. Livingston, would you rather w..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ms. Livingston, would you rather we continue to march toward Thornbourgh so that we can sign the treaty there?"
entries.menuText: "Ms. Livingston, would you rather we continue to march toward Thornbourgh so that we can sign the treaty there?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I don't think you are in any posit..."
entries.dialogueText: "I don't think you are in any position to negotiate."
entries.menuText: "I don't think you are in any position to negotiate."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Ms. Livingston, I can replace you..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ms. Livingston, I can replace you with someone else and have that person sign the treaty instead."
entries.menuText: "Ms. Livingston, I can replace you with someone else and have that person sign the treaty instead."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""I will remember this, Rumburg will..."
entries.dialogueText: "I will remember this, Rumburg will remember this."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Part I... Section II... Reparation..."
entries.dialogueText: "Part I... Section II... Reparations... "

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Sordland's government and its alli..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sordland's government and its allies affirm and Rumburg accepts the responsibility for causing for the losses and damages..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Section V... Sordland's Front...""
entries.dialogueText: "Section V... Sordland's Front..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You want us to pay reparations for..."
entries.dialogueText: "You want us to pay reparations for a war that you declared!"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""This is outrageous!""
entries.dialogueText: "This is outrageous!"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Rumburg will immediately surrender..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rumburg will immediately surrender the cities of Tzarsbourgh, Dome, and their respective surrounding territories to the Republic of Sordland."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You want our two major cities in t..."
entries.dialogueText: "You want our two major cities in the south? This will cripple us for years to come."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Rumburg will immediately surrender..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rumburg will immediately surrender the city of Tzarsbourgh and its surrounding territories to the Republic of Sordland."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""...recognizing the moral obligatio..."
entries.dialogueText: "...recognizing the moral obligation to redress the wrong done by Rumburg in 1921, both to the rights of Agnolia and to the wishes of the population of Dome..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Section VII... Dome...""
entries.dialogueText: "Section VII... Dome..."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""The territories shall be restored..."
entries.dialogueText: "The territories shall be restored to the Republic of Agnolia... "

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You want our two major cities in t..."
entries.dialogueText: "You want our two major cities in the south? This will cripple us for years to come."

entries.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
entries.title: Maartin Van Hoorten: ""It is only natural that you return..."
entries.dialogueText: "It is only natural that you return what you have taken from us."

entries.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
entries.title: Maartin Van Hoorten: ""The people of Dome will finally be..."
entries.dialogueText: "The people of Dome will finally be freed from your tyrannical rule."

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: ""Oh, it's not done yet, *my Queen*.""
entries.dialogueText: "Oh, it's not done yet, *my Queen*."

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: ""Have a look at Section IX. I belie..."
entries.dialogueText: "Have a look at Section IX. I believe it is titled 'The Wehzek People'."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Rumburg will immediately surrender..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rumburg will immediately surrender the territories surrounding Datefort to Wehlen in accordance with the wishes of the Wehzek people living in these territories."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""What is this madness? What about a..."
entries.dialogueText: "What is this madness? What about all the Rumburgian and Bludish people living there?"

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: ""That is none of your business.""
entries.dialogueText: "That is none of your business."

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: ""I'm sure that my friend Anton and..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm sure that my friend Anton and I can come to another agreement similar to the last one."

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: ""I'm sure that President Rayne and..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm sure that President Rayne and I can come to another agreement similar to the last one."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You not only intended to commit a..."
entries.dialogueText: "You not only intended to commit a genocide of the Bludish people, but of Rumburgians as well. I won't stand for this."

entries.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
entries.title: Wiktor Smolak: ""That will depend on how they behav..."
entries.dialogueText: "That will depend on how they behave, don't you agree?"

entries.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
entries.title: Emmerich Hegel: ""You won't be in any position to wo..."
entries.dialogueText: "You won't be in any position to worry about that."

entries.speaker: Emmerich Hegel
entries.title: Emmerich Hegel: ""It is due time to free the Rumburg..."
entries.dialogueText: "It is due time to free the Rumburgian people from your tyrannical rule. The workers' revolution is about to begin."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Section X... The People's Revoluti..."
entries.dialogueText: "Section X... The People's Revolution.... The Queen of Rumburg will immediately abdicate and transfer her authority to the newly established National Liberation Committee that will be elected by the people."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""The Republic of Valgsland, as a re..."
entries.dialogueText: "The Republic of Valgsland, as a representative of the CSP, will work closely with Rumburg's new government to advise and oversee this transition of power."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""You want to destroy Rumburg with y..."
entries.dialogueText: "You want to destroy Rumburg with your poisonous ideology."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I don't think you are in any posit..."
entries.dialogueText: "I don't think you are in any position to negotiate."
entries.menuText: "I don't think you are in any position to negotiate."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Ms. Livingston, it seems you do no..."
entries.dialogueText: “Ms. Livingston, it seems you do not fully comprehend the situation. We are not asking!"
entries.menuText: “Ms. Livingston, it seems you do not fully comprehend the situation. We are not asking!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Ms. Livingston, would you rather w..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ms. Livingston, would you rather we continue our march towards Thornbourgh so that we can sign the treaty there?"
entries.menuText: "Ms. Livingston, would you rather we continue our march towards Thornbourgh so that we can sign the treaty there?"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""I will remember this. Rumburg will..."
entries.dialogueText: "I will remember this. Rumburg will remember this."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Ms. Livingston, we can always repl..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ms. Livingston, we can always replace you with someone else and have that person sign the treaty instead."
entries.menuText: "Ms. Livingston, we can always replace you with someone else and have that person sign the treaty instead."

entries.speaker: Patricio Alvarez
entries.title: Patricio Alvarez: ""Ms. Livingston, we only want to as..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ms. Livingston, we only want to assure peace in the region."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Section X... Status of Forces Agre..."
entries.dialogueText: "Section X... Status of Forces Agreement... Rumburg grants, and ATO accepts, the right, upon the coming into force of this Treaty, to deploy ATO land, air and sea forces in and about Rumburg."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""During the exercise of the right ...."
entries.dialogueText: "During the exercise of the right ... Rumburg will not grant, without the prior consent of ATO, any bases or any rights, powers or authority whatsoever, in or relating to bases or the right of garrison or of maneuver, or transit of ground, air or naval forces to any third power."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Do you realize what this will do t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Do you realize what this will do to us? We'll lose our freedom, our ability to defend ourselves, our economic independence..."

entries.speaker: Patricio Alvarez
entries.title: Patricio Alvarez: ""That's not all. You missed a coupl..."
entries.dialogueText: "That's not all. You missed a couple of points from Section II, Reparation. Let me summarize it for you."

entries.speaker: Patricio Alvarez
entries.title: Patricio Alvarez: ""According to Section II, Rumburg w..."
entries.dialogueText: "According to Section II, Rumburg will remove all tariffs on Lespian products being sold in any Rumburgian territories."

entries.speaker: Patricio Alvarez
entries.title: Patricio Alvarez: ""The Republic of Lespia will have p..."
entries.dialogueText: "The Republic of Lespia will have priority access to Rumburg's market."

entries.speaker: Patricio Alvarez
entries.title: Patricio Alvarez: ""Furthermore, all Lespian companies..."
entries.dialogueText: "Furthermore, all Lespian companies established in any territories of Rumburg will enjoy a 10-year tax-free period."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Wait, what's this?""
entries.dialogueText: "Wait, what's this?"

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Wait, what's this?""
entries.dialogueText: "Wait, what's this?"

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I raised my middle finger in the Qu..."
entries.dialogueText: I raised my middle finger in the Queen's face.
entries.menuText: Give her the middle finger.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""That's from my son.""
entries.dialogueText: "That's from my son."
entries.menuText: "That's from my son."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""My parting gift from Sordland.""
entries.dialogueText: "My parting gift from Sordland."
entries.menuText: "My parting gift from Sordland."

entries.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
entries.title: Beatrice Livingston: ""Well, I never...""
entries.dialogueText: "Well, I never..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Of course, the real credit goes to..."
entries.dialogueText: "Of course, the real credit goes to Colonel Tarquin Soll, who selflessly came out of retirement to aid in the war plans."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Credit as well goes to Foreign Min..."
entries.dialogueText: "Credit as well goes to Foreign Minister Deivid Wisci, whose insight into Sordland's allies proved invaluable. He certainly deserves a long and peaceful retirement."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She laid out the treaty and began t..."
entries.dialogueText: She laid out the treaty and began to read the document.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: ""Defense minister Iosef Lancea was..."
entries.dialogueText: "Defense minister Iosef Lancea was the man of the hour as his superior strategies broke the morale of the enemy at Dome. Following that operation, our troops were victorious in their assaults towards their capital and tipped the scales in our favor. Soon after, they were routing the enemy in the fields around Thornbourgh...'
